main_text.head: Hoc Epigramma ISAACVS CASAVBONVS ex Græco sic elegantissimè & felicissimè Latinè vertit.
main_text.p: Heu! quis Vita auctorem te suffulit? heu? Quisve salutem hominum perdere te potuit? Non Caiphas adeo, non oscula perfida Iudæ, Aut, Pilate, tua, consceleratæ manus: Consilia ut Patris, propriaque & clementia mentis, Dum tua, te miserans, improba facta luo. Iudicium iudex subis! indomitusque domaris! Nil patiens pateris! non moriens moreris! Quippe creator ego atque creatus, homoque, Deusque, Nil patiens patior, non moriens morior. Mortem ita morte dedi morti: latissima præbent Gaudia cœligenis, gaudia terrigenis. Alta o mentis opus! diuina o consilia! istud Cœligenæque stupent, terrigenæque stupent. I nunc, Orce niger: Sathan, & tu perditor, i nunc: Ipsa viden? vita mors tua facta via est.
main_text.head: In Pseudocleri Romani votiuum cœlibatum.
main_text.p: Romana in primis abigat quùCuria quotquot Legitimi iurant fœdera sancta thori. Cur, age, cur patres cupiunt fratresque vocari, Quotquot alit summi Curia Pontificis?

page.notes: Verse lines in italic alternate with roman as printed; the Latin in the first heading is printed in a larger mixed type. Some words are doubtful in the scan, notably "subis", "Orce", "quùCuria" and "votiuum", which are copied as printed. The first verse block is printed with an alternating italic and roman line pattern and each line is a verse line; the text is given as running verse paragraphs.
